codeReview.summary: Commit `2db3177` fixes the round-1 blockers in the touched backend files (`part64/scripts/*`, `world_life.py`, `constants.py`, `attribution.py`, and `test_agent_runtime.py`), but it does not clear the remaining blocking regressions from `update-api-and-records`. The checked-in frontend still targets removed `/api/muse/*` and `/api/witness*` routes and still ignores the renamed `agent_events` WebSocket payload, so the full backend-refactor scrutiny failure set is not resolved.

issues.description: The checked-in frontend still targets removed backend routes (`/api/muse/message`, plus `/api/muse/create`, `/api/muse/sync-pins`, `/api/muse/threat-radar/*`, and `/api/witness*` in `App.tsx`, `ThreatRadarPanel.tsx`, `Chat.tsx`, and `Canvas.tsx`). The current server only serves `/api/agent/*`, `/api/continuity*`, and `/api/attribution`, so the client/server contract break flagged in the original `update-api-and-records` review remains unresolved.

`useWorldState` still branches only on `muse_events`, but the backend now emits `agent_events` from `part64/code/world_web/server.py`. Live agent-event updates are still dropped by the checked-in frontend, so the WebSocket regression from the original `update-api-and-records` review remains.

blockingIssues.description: Frontend callers still use removed HTTP routes after the backend rename.
blockingIssues.evidence: `part64/frontend/src/app/useChatCommandHandlers.ts:182` posts to `/api/muse/message`; `part64/frontend/src/App.tsx:632,1121,1216,2263`, `part64/frontend/src/components/Panels/ThreatRadarPanel.tsx:133,203`, `part64/frontend/src/components/Panels/Chat.tsx:519`, and `part64/frontend/src/components/Simulation/Canvas.tsx:5890` still call `/api/muse/*` or `/api/witness*`. The backend only defines `/api/agent/*`, `/api/continuity*`, and `/api/attribution` at `part64/code/world_web/server.py:9067-11773`.

blockingIssues.description: Frontend WebSocket handling still listens for the removed `muse_events` message type.
blockingIssues.evidence: `part64/frontend/src/hooks/useWorldState.ts:424` checks only `msgType === 'muse_events'`, while `part64/code/world_web/server.py:7162` and `7205` now send `"type": "agent_events"`.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared architecture docs still describe the pre-refactor backend modules and API contract, which makes cross-surface review of rename work harder than it should be.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/library/architecture.md:23-24,45` still lists `lore.py`, `myth_bridge.py`, and REST endpoints `/api/myth` / `/api/muse/*`, while `.factory/library/naming-map.md:66-68` and `part64/code/world_web/server.py:9067-11773` use `/api/attribution`, `/api/agent/*`, and `/api/continuity`.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `refactor-worker` still does not explicitly require checking checked-in client consumers when backend API/event names change, so a backend-only rename can still be handed off as complete while the repository's own frontend remains incompatible.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/skills/refactor-worker/SKILL.md:28-31` requires running backend `test_python_*` commands and `SKILL.md:71` says to curl API endpoints, but it never asks workers to inspect checked-in consumers. The unresolved callers remain in `part64/frontend/src/app/useChatCommandHandlers.ts:182`, `part64/frontend/src/components/Panels/ThreatRadarPanel.tsx:133,203`, `part64/frontend/src/components/Panels/Chat.tsx:519`, `part64/frontend/src/App.tsx:632,1121,1216,2263`, `part64/frontend/src/components/Simulation/Canvas.tsx:5890`, and `part64/frontend/src/hooks/useWorldState.ts:424`.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission/shared-service guidance still treats `python3 -m code.tests.test_*` as definitive test execution even though several important backend test modules do not self-execute under that command.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Mission `AGENTS.md:20,64` and `.factory/services.yaml:7-10` prescribe `python3 -m code.tests.test_*`. The fix worker transcript for session `723e59da-e022-4afe-bc3b-b684476973b9` records discovering this gap while debugging `test_agent_runtime.py`, and current grep shows `part64/code/tests/test_world_life.py`, `part64/code/tests/test_attribution.py`, and `part64/code/tests/test_world_web_pm2.py` still have no `if __name__ == "__main__":`, while `part64/code/tests/test_agent_runtime.py:816` now does.

keyFindings: `git show --stat --oneline 2db3177` shows the fix commit only touched backend/scripts/test files; it did not update any frontend callers.

Current backend code confirms the targeted round-1 backend fixes landed: `part64/scripts/*` has no residual `daimoi` references, `part64/code/world_life.py` now uses `logger_aya`/`boost`, `part64/code/world_web/constants.py:2500` now uses `nexus.ui.system_overview`, and `part64/code/attribution.py:113` now reads `ATTRIBUTION_URL`.

Current frontend code still demonstrates the unresolved contract break identified in the original `update-api-and-records` review: old `/api/muse/*` and `/api/witness*` callers remain, and `useWorldState` still ignores `agent_events`.

addressesFailureFrom.notes: `part64/scripts/bench_cdb_vs_python.py`, `ensure_npu_embeddings.py`, `eval_sim_learning_suite.py`, and `homeostasis_soak_probe.py` were updated to particle-era imports/keys, and `rg 'daimoi' part64/scripts/` is now clean.
`part64/code/world_life.py:34-111` now uses neutral actor ids and the `boost` action, and `part64/code/world_web/constants.py:2500` now uses `nexus.ui.system_overview`.

The original frontend/backend contract break is still present: frontend callers continue to use `/api/muse/*` and `/api/witness*`, and the frontend still listens for `muse_events` while the server emits `agent_events`.
`part64/code/tests/test_agent_runtime.py` now uses `agent_id`, `list_agents()`, `agent.*` event names, `presence_type == "agent"`, and includes a `__main__` runner for direct execution.

summary: Fix review failed. `2db3177` resolves the five backend-side issues it targeted, but the two original blocking `update-api-and-records` contract regressions are still present in the checked-in frontend, so `fix-backend-scrutiny-issues` does not fully clear the prior backend-refactor scrutiny failures.
